questions.text: What is the purpose of providing a fallback value in the `var()` function for CSS custom properties?
distractors: To reduce the amount of CSS code.
To improve performance in modern browsers.

questions.answer: To ensure a valid value is applied if the custom property is undefined.

questions.text:
How would the following declaration behave?

```css
color: var(--main-color, var(--fallback-color, #000));
```
distractors: It will apply `--main-color` even if it is not defined, defaulting to that value.
It will apply `--main-color` and `--fallback-color` simultaneously, resulting in a blend of the two colors.
It will always default to `#000`, regardless of whether `--main-color` or `--fallback-color` is defined.
questions.answer: It applies `--main-color` if defined; otherwise, checks `--fallback-color;` and if both are undefined, it uses `#000`.

questions.text: What is one benefit of using `@property` in CSS?
distractors: It improves performance by precomputing custom property values.

questions.text: In the declaration of a custom `@property`, what does the `initial-value` specify?

The priority of the property in the cascade.
